headline: Iran says supertanker with 2 million barrels of oil sank in Gulf
summary: Iran said a supertanker carrying 2 million barrels of oil sank in the Gulf. Tehran has made multiple recent announcements of ships catching fire in the strait, often claiming they struck mines.
why: The Gulf and the Strait of Hormuz carry a large share of seaborne oil, so disruptions there can quickly affect crude prices and tanker insurance costs.
why_moved: Reported loss of a supertanker carrying 2 million barrels, in a strait where ships have recently reported fires and mine strikes, raises concern about crude supply and shipping risk.
